alex: hey all, first-week onboarding snag. i built the runtime from source and when i run a small smoke invocation the process crashes before main: looks like a ctor in a shared lib calling NVML during dlopen. any tips?

alex: run output:

alex: ```
$ bazel run //runtime/examples:kv_smoke
INFO: Running kv_smoke
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
#0  0x7f6d8a3b2c in ?? () from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1
#1  0x55a1b2c3d4 in runtime::gpu::DeviceTracker::DeviceTracker()
#2  0x55a1b2c3a0 in __static_initialization_and_destruction_0
```

alex: `ldd` on the runtime lib shows libnvidia-ml.so.1 => not found. i created a symlink to the versioned file but still crash because it looks like the ctor runs while dlopen resolves symbols.

mika: welcome! this is a common new-hire trap. two quick facts: 1) some tests/binaries dlopen the runtime with RTLD_NOW which forces immediate symbol resolution and can trigger NVML probes in ctors; 2) dev containers sometimes don't have the correct driver libs mounted so dlopen fails or returns a different ABI.

tiago: try preloading the host driver lib so ctor sees the expected symbols: `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.535.86 bazel run ...` or run the container with `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` mounted. also `readelf -d bazel-bin/runtime/libredwood_runtime.so | grep NEEDED` will show if NVML is a direct dependency.

alex: tried LD_PRELOAD pointing to the host lib, ldd now resolves but still crashes; backtrace points into nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex_v2.

mika: that suggests either ABI mismatch (driver <-> lib) or our ctor calling NVML too early. quick dev fixes: - set `NVML_INJECTION_DISABLED=1` for local runs to skip NVML probes; - run under gdb to get full bt: `gdb --args bazel-bin/runtime/examples/kv_smoke` then `run` and `bt`; - grep for globals that call DeviceTracker in ctors (`git grep "DeviceTracker::DeviceTracker"`).

tiago: another workaround is to change the dlopen flags in the small launcher to use RTLD_LAZY if possible so ctor init order is different, but that requires a code change. for onboarding you can also run on infra's dev-gpu node that mounts drivers correctly.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-523: "onboard: runtime ctor NVML call segfault in dev container" assigned to infra oncall. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-523 :ticket:

devex-bot: FYI — onboarding doc updated with a note about NVML/driver libs and the `NVML_INJECTION_DISABLED` env var: https://redwood.dev/onboarding/runtime-dev#gpu-drivers :memo:

alex: thanks — i'll gdb, grep for early DeviceTracker uses, and link the ticket if infra needs to mount drivers. appreciate the pointers :thumbsup:
